sections.h2: Selling a house in Sumter, South Carolina
sections.html:
Sumter sits near the center of South Carolina, about 45 miles east of Columbia and about 100 miles north of Charleston. It is the county seat of Sumter County. The city had 43,463 residents at the 2020 count and an estimate of 43,094 for July 1, 2025.

About 57.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $199,100 for 2020 to 2024. That is a citywide figure, not a price for any one street. The other 42.8 percent of homes are not owner-occupied, so a good share of local sellers are landlords, heirs of a rental, or owners who already moved out.

Shaw Air Force Base and the county's plants and hospitals mean some owners have to move on a fixed date, after orders or a new job. Those sellers often can't sit through a long listing period, which is why cash closings come up so often here.

Sumter has long, hot summers and about 48.8 inches of rain a year, so roofs, air conditioning and moisture are the usual trouble spots. A house that sat vacant through several wet summers can pick up mold, soft subfloors or a failing roof. Those repairs are what usually push owners toward an as-is sale.

Parts of town fall in the Sumter Historic District or the Stateburg Historic District, and the city has a Design Review Board. If your house is in an older district, ask the planning office whether exterior changes need review before you start work.

The Wateree River runs along the western edge of the county, and Lake Marion and other waterways touch it too. If your property is near water, ask the city or county about flood zone status before you list, because a buyer's lender will check it.

The City of Sumter handles building permits, code enforcement, planning and zoning, and water, sewer and sanitation service from its offices at 21 N. Main Street, phone (803) 436-2500.

  • Building permits: Pull a permit before repair work, and ask about open permits before closing.
  • Code enforcement: This department handles litter reports and the Sumter Pride Program. Call about an overgrown lot, a violation notice or an unpermitted addition.
  • Planning and zoning: This office supports the Board of Zoning Appeals, the Design Review Board and the Planning Commission.
  • Utilities: The city runs water, wastewater, stormwater and sanitation. Owners start or stop water service through the city.

Ask each office what is open on your address before you list or sign a contract. An open permit or a violation can stall a closing late in the process.

Deeds are recorded at the Sumter County Register of Deeds in the courthouse at 141 N. Main Street. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the number is 803-436-2177.

The office records deeds, mortgages, plats, liens and powers of attorney. It does not prepare forms, give legal advice or run title searches, and staff will not fill out a deed for you, so use a closing attorney.

South Carolina charges a deed recording fee of $1.85 for each $500 of value, split into $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. The seller is generally liable for it, and the buyer is liable second.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The county Treasurer, at 13 East Canal Street, bills property taxes one year in arrears. Notices go out each October and are payable by January 15 with no penalty.

Payment datePenalty added to base tax
After January 153%
After February 110%
After March 1615%

Because bills run in arrears, an unpaid prior-year bill has to be settled at or before a Sumter closing. Ask the Treasurer for the current balance before you list, and bring that figure to your closing attorney.

Sumter owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. Each route changes the timeline and decides who pays for repairs. A traditional listing brings the most exposure but depends on a buyer's lender, an appraisal and often an inspection repair list.

A cash sale removes the lender step. We buy houses as-is, so cleanout, deferred repairs and a tenant situation don't have to be fixed first, and the closing date is set around your plans.

  • Inherited house with several heirs in or outside South Carolina
  • Rental with a tenant still in place
  • Home with deferred roof, plumbing or HVAC work
  • Owner relocating for a job or military move

sections.h2: How a cash sale works, step by step
sections.html:
You send us the address and a few details about the house and any tenant. We look at the property and make an offer. You decide whether to take it, and there is no obligation if you say no.

If you accept, a closing attorney or title company checks the title, confirms any taxes or liens, and prepares the deed. You choose the closing date, which can be quick if title is clear or later if you need time to move. At closing the unpaid tax balance and any payoff come out of your proceeds, and the deed is recorded at the Register of Deeds.

Ask for the offer in writing and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, carrying costs and the wait for a buyer's financing. Gather the deed, your latest tax notice, any mortgage statement and tenant lease before you talk to anyone, so the numbers are real.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Sumter, SC?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A cash sale can close in days to a few weeks once title is clear, while a listing needs time for showings, a buyer's financing and an appraisal. Either way the deed is recorded at the Sumter County Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Who records the deed in Sumter County?
faqs.a: The Sumter County Register of Deeds at the courthouse, 141 N. Main Street. The office doesn't prepare documents or give legal advice, so a closing attorney usually handles the deed.

faqs.q: When are Sumter County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property taxes are due by January 15 with no penalty. Penalties of 3 percent, 10 percent and 15 percent are added after January 15, February 1 and March 16.

faqs.q: Do I need to make repairs before selling a Sumter house for cash?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is, so repairs, cleanout and old code issues don't need to be finished first. Closing an open city violation can still help any sale go smoothly.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sumter house that has a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Landlords can sell a rental with the tenant in place. South Carolina law relieves a landlord who conveys the property in a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser of later liability once the tenant is told in writing. The landlord stays responsible for the security deposit unless it is transferred and the tenant is notified.
